h1.u: 103 in view of Rylander and Szunerits

body.p: Claims 1-3, 5, 30, 37, 42, 43, 47, and1 35-141 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Rylander, et al., U.S. Pat. Apl. Pub. No. 2013/0338627 ("Rylander") in view of Szunerits, et al., "Sensing using Localised Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensors," ChemComm., 48(72):8999-9010, 2012 ("Szunerits"). The Office Action states that Rylander generally teaches claim 1, except that Rylander does not teach that the immobilized particles are positioned in an optically interrogatable position with respect to light transmitted through the member to the end portion. The Office Action then argues that such particles are taught in Szunerits.

Initially, it is not seen how or why one of ordinary skill in the art would have sought to have immobilized a particle to the device taught in Rylander. Rylander is generally directed to a minimally-invasive fiber optic microneedle device-which physically penetrates tissue to deliver light (Abstract). The Rylander structure is described a light guiding microneedle at microscales that is used for tissue imaging or laser therapy (see, e.g., paragraph 0035). Rylander teaches that such microneedles are difficult to insert into the skin, and thus, a support member for increasing the critical buckling force of the needle(s) to fortify the needles for insertion into the skin is taught in paragraph 0032. For example, the microneedle may be embedded inside an elastic medium such as a polymer. Other examples include a guidance ferrule template and an elastomeric support material for increasing the buckling force of the needle(s). See, e.g., paragraph 0035. In addition, Fig. 1 schematically shows that the microneedle is directly inserting into the skin (through various skin layers), while Fig. 4 provides a series of photographic images of a microneedle inserted into the skin.
Under such conditions, it is not seen how or why one of ordinary skill in the art would have had any motivation to immobilize a particle onto the microneedle, or would have been able to do so

with a reasonable expectation of success. Given such forces (which are described in even more detail on pages 15-16 of Rylander), any such immobilized particle on the microneedle would have been quickly "scraped off' as the microneedle was inserted into the skin. Thus, there would have been no rational or logical reason for adding a particle to the microneedles of Rylander. Instead, the reasonable expectation would have been that adding any such particles to Rylander would have been a futile exercise, since there would have been no way to prevent those particles from being "scraped off' and therefore lost.

With respect to Szunerits, although Szunerits teaches the use of particles in surface plasma resonance, it is not seen where Szunerits teaches or suggests immobilizing particles to the end portion of a member, as is recited in claim 1. Rather, Szunerits teaches that the particles are linked to surfaces, which are then optically interrogated via surface plasmon resonance (see, e.g., the abstract of Szunerits). For example, as is shown in Fig. 1D, a series of metallic nanostructures (gold) are shown attached to a glass surface, which is then studied using a UV/VIS spectrometer. Accordingly, it is not seen how or why one of ordinary skill in the art would have arrived at at least one particle immobilized relative to the end portion of the member, as is recited in claim 1, when combining Rylander and Szunerits, as neither reference teaches or suggests such a structure. Furthermore, even assuming arguendo that such a structure is taught, it is not seen how or why one of ordinary skill in the art would have combined Rylander and Szunerits, as the techniques in Rylander (inserting needles into the skin) would have caused any such particles to be "scraped off." Furthermore, Rylander nowhere teaches or suggests that such systems could have reasonably been used for surface plasma resonance, as the skin does not have a transparent surface, which is required for surface plasma resonance to occur. Thus, it is believed that the combination of Rylander and Szunerits is improper, and withdrawal of this rejection is respectfully requested.

In view of the foregoing remarks, this application should now be in condition for allowance. A notice to this effect is respectfully requested.
